description: Review round 1 of stoa-90tpd implementation. Reviewers file findings as children of this epic.
notes:
Confidence: 5% chance of missed P0 bug. The four implementation areas reviewed are sound: is_loopback_addr correctly parses IPv4/IPv6/localhost with fail-safe defaults; is_loopback_url_host correctly strips scheme and handles bracketed IPv6; RuntimeEnvironment.from_env() defaults to Production on unrecognised input (fail-safe); the three guard blocks in reader/mail/imap main.rs all correctly gate on is_dev_mode() && !is_loopback_addr() and call process::exit(1). The is_dev_mode() definition in auth/src/config.rs is thorough — it covers all six credential sources (users, credential_file, client_certs, trusted_issuers, oidc_providers) so there is no bypass path. The one real finding (stoa-cajkm.1) is correctly filed at P1: duplicated guard message strings with divergent wording is a genuine maintainability risk with a concrete current example (imap omits the second fix option). There is no engineering basis to label it opinion. No P0 bug found. Running out of real complaints: yes.
Maintainer risk: MEDIUM. Five real findings filed (stoa-cajkm.1, stoa-cajkm.3, stoa-cajkm.9, stoa-cajkm.12, stoa-cajkm.18). The most concrete bugs-in-waiting are: (a) the private is_loopback_addr copy in sieve_admin.rs that will miss future fixes to the canonical version, and (b) the 5x startup banner duplication where any field addition requires 5 coordinated edits. The dev-mode guard message divergence is already visible — imap's message already differs from reader's and mail's. No P0 correctness bugs found in this set of changes; all issues are maintenance-burden class.
title: Review round 1: Dev mode startup guard (stoa-90tpd)
